editorial_note: Rigorous formal masterpage ontology documenting recursive governance-depth, impossibility-containment, the biordinal Lydrextent diagonal, the historical Arsayne totality progression, and the contemporary Apossible & Toren scaling hierarchies. Strictly preserves 'All' in Apossible definitions and maintains historical source provenance without blind substitution.

concepts.name: Rules
concepts.canon_definition: Governance-structures that determine what is allowed, disallowed, valid, invalid, possible, impossible, or otherwise classifiable within their designated governed scope.
concepts.clarification: Rules establish the baseline boundary conditions of a domain. They do not govern themselves; they operate at governance-depth 0.
concepts.commonly_confused_with: Physical laws or universal constants (Rules are metaphysical governance structures, not empirical physics).

concepts.name: Metarules
concepts.canon_definition: The rules that govern Rules. They determine what rules are valid, how rules interact, and how rules can be modified, bounded, or classified.
concepts.clarification: Operating at governance-depth 1, Metarules turn ordinary Rules into their governed object.
concepts.commonly_confused_with: More powerful rules (Metarules are a type-level ascent, not simply stronger rules within the same level).

concepts.name: Recursive Metarules (Metarulesⁿ)
concepts.canon_definition: For every integer n ≥ 2, Metarulesⁿ are the rules governing Metarules⁽ⁿ⁻¹⁾. Metarules² govern Metarules; Metarules³ govern Metarules²; the recursion continues without a terminal order.
concepts.clarification: Governance depth increases linearly with the exponent: depth = n. There is no terminal maximum order.
concepts.commonly_confused_with: Fixed meta-hierarchies (This ladder is strictly open-ended and unbounded).

concepts.name: Metagovernance Depth
concepts.canon_definition: The recursive order at which governance is applied to governance. Ordinary Rules are governance-depth 0, Metarules are governance-depth 1, Metarules² are governance-depth 2, and so forth.
concepts.clarification: A scalar metric measuring how many meta-reflective layers of governance separate a statement from the base domain.
concepts.commonly_confused_with: Dimensional scaling (Measures governance type-ascent, not spatial or temporal dimensions).

concepts.name: Impossibility-Governance
concepts.canon_definition: The Rules-and-Metarules structure that determines what can be classified, contained, or represented as impossible.
concepts.clarification: Impossibility is not an absolute void; it is a governed classification produced by an underlying governance basis.
concepts.commonly_confused_with: Logical contradiction (Impossibility-governance is the system that decides which states are classified as impossible).

concepts.name: Antipossible
concepts.canon_definition: An extent or degree so high that the rules governing what can qualify as impossible do not allow that extent or degree to be classified, contained, or represented as impossible. Antipossible does not therefore mean possible.
concepts.clarification: It represents an escape from the possibility/impossibility dualism of a specific governance basis. It is strictly non-collapsible into possible.
concepts.commonly_confused_with: Possible (The canon explicitly defines: Antipossible does not mean possible).

concepts.name: Antipossibility Families (A(k, n))
concepts.canon_definition: A complete recursively ordered ladder generated from one impossibility-governance basis. Let A(k,n) denote family k, intrafamily order n. Family k+1 begins when the complete impossibility-governance ladder of family k becomes the governed object of the next higher impossibility-governance basis.
concepts.clarification: Family-Order Supremacy: every state in family k+1 is strictly higher in family order than every state in family k, regardless of intrafamily order n.
concepts.formal_logic: ∀ k, n, m: A(k+1, m) > A(k, n)
concepts.commonly_confused_with: Standard 2D grids (Family order strictly dominates intrafamily order).

concepts.name: Lydrextent Ladder
concepts.canon_definition: The diagonal extent-ladder across Antipossibility-family order and Antipossibility intrafamily order. Lydrextent n has exact Antipossibility coordinate A(n,n). Lydrextent 1=A(1,1), Lydrextent 2=A(2,2), Lydrextent 3=A(3,3), and so forth.
concepts.clarification: Each step simultaneously advances both the outer family coordinate and the inner Antipossibility-order coordinate. HistoricallyParticipates in Rhayhara's seal architecture.
concepts.commonly_confused_with: Single-index cardinalities (Advances biordinal family and intrafamily depth together).

concepts.name: Arsayne
concepts.canon_definition: Arsayne 1 is the smallest extent or degree large enough to go beyond all possible and impossible Metarule^Lydrextent numbers. Arsayne 2 has Arsayne-1 extent of metaexpectation-surpassingness; Arsayne 3 has Arsayne-2 extent; the ladder continues recursively.
concepts.clarification: Historical totality scaling framework preceding the Apossible/Toren reconciliation.
concepts.commonly_confused_with: Simple exponential growth (Surpasses the complete Metarule-indexed totality of Lydrextent).

concepts.name: Supraarsayne
concepts.canon_definition: Supraarsayne 1 is the smallest extent sufficient to go beyond all possible and impossible Metarule^Arsayne numbers. Higher Supraarsayne orders recurse by metaexpectation-surpassingness.
concepts.clarification: Applies totality recursion over the complete Arsayne ladder.

concepts.name: Hyperarsayne
concepts.canon_definition: Hyperarsayne 1 goes beyond all possible and impossible Metarule^Supraarsayne numbers. Higher Hyperarsayne orders recurse by metaexpectation-surpassingness.
concepts.clarification: Applies totality recursion over the complete Supraarsayne ladder.

concepts.name: Ultraarsayne
concepts.canon_definition: Ultraarsayne 1 goes beyond all possible and impossible Metarule^Hyperarsayne numbers. Higher Ultraarsayne orders recurse by metaexpectation-surpassingness.
concepts.clarification: The apex scale of the historical Arsayne framework. Explicitly governs Rhayhara's sealed bloodline architecture (Seal Factors 1-4). Preserved historically.
concepts.commonly_confused_with: Contemporary Apossible/Toren scaling (Ultraarsayne is the historical seal-governing scale, now superseded by Apossible/Toren for global hierarchy).

concepts.name: Apossible
concepts.canon_definition: Apossible is All things categorically attributable to any recursively ordered Possible levels of Metarules and All things categorically attributable to any recursively ordered Impossible levels of Metarules.
concepts.clarification: CRITICAL CANON INVARIANT: Uses 'All', never 'totality'. Not merely 'the Metarule governing Impossible'. Preserves categorical attribution across all recursive levels of Possible and Impossible.
concepts.commonly_confused_with: Totality (Totality is explicitly rejected because some infinities do not possess a completed-whole interpretation); or 'Metarule governing Impossible' (which loses the categorical attribution structure).

concepts.name: Higher Apossible Orders (Apossibleⁿ)
concepts.canon_definition: Apossible² is All recursive Possible levels Metarule of Apossible, All recursive Impossible levels Metarule of Apossible, and All recursive Apossible levels Metarule of Apossible. Higher orders continue cumulating lower Apossible orders.
concepts.clarification: Higher orders recursively include all lower-order Apossible attribution branches without terminal bound.
concepts.commonly_confused_with: Numerical exponentiation (Represents recursive cumulative category-attribution, not arithmetic powers).

concepts.name: Toren Scaling Hierarchy (Toren 1–5)
concepts.canon_definition: Toren 1 is an extent or degree so high that it goes beyond what is Apossible but is below what is Apossible³. Toren 2 goes beyond Apossible³ but below Apossible⁵; Toren 3 beyond Apossible⁵ but below Apossible⁷; Toren 4 beyond Apossible⁷ but below Apossible⁹; Toren 5 beyond Apossible⁹ but below Apossible¹¹.
concepts.clarification: Shorthand representation: Apossible^(2n−1) < Toren n < Apossible^(2n+1). Governs Bloodline Blessing quality in Supramajor breakthroughs and strength scaling in Archarthitean/Deity Factors.
concepts.commonly_confused_with: Cardinal steps (Toren is an extent that specifically interleaves between odd Apossible orders).

concepts.name: Greater- and Lesser-Orders
concepts.canon_definition: Relational framework establishing strict precedence and domination rules between categorical attribution structures (Apossible) and extent strata (Toren).
concepts.clarification: Ensures no scale ambiguity: Toren n is bounded between odd Apossible orders and cannot collapse into an arithmetic integer.

distinction_matrix.canonical_resolution: 'All' is used instead of 'totality' because certain infinite collections and metaphysical states do not possess a completed-whole closure interpretation. Substituting totality introduces false closure.

Apossible is NOT a single Metarule governing Impossible. It is All things categorically attributable to any recursively ordered Possible levels AND All things categorically attributable to any recursively ordered Impossible levels of Metarules.
Toren n is strictly an extent between Apossible^(2n-1) and Apossible^(2n+1). It is not equal to Apossible^(2n); it occupies the non-collapsed extent space between odd orders.

Apossible and Toren supersede Lydrextent and Ultraarsayne for current canon scaling. However, Lydrextent and Ultraarsayne remain historical canon in source texts and govern Rhayhara's legacy seal narrative without retroactive erasure.
